**Al-Nassr roll into this one as clear favorites, and honestly, they should be — Diriyah's defending has looked shaky all season.** 🔵

Al-Nassr are clicking with three wins in their last five, even if that loss to Al-Ittihad stung. Diriyah, meanwhile, are grinding out results (2W 2D 1L) but haven't exactly been a fortress—a 0-2 hammering at home to Al-Qadsiah last time out tells you something.

Key storylines:

- **Cristiano Ronaldo** gets a home crowd boost at Al-Awwal Park; Diriyah's backline has leaked goals and won't relish tracking him
- **Al-Nassr's midfield dominance** with A. Al-Khaibari and Ângelo should control tempo against a Diriyah side that's been vulnerable in transitions
- Diriyah need **G. Laborde** to lead the line with real sharpness—they've scored just once in their last two, so coming to Riyadh won't get easier

Expected lineups:

- **Al-Nassr**: Bento, S. Alnajdi, I. Martínez, M. Simakan, N. Boushal, A. Al-Khaibari, Ângelo, S. Costa, S. Mané, C. Ronaldo, A. Yahya
- **Diriyah**: N. Vasilj, H. Alsebyani, B. Djimsiti, Q. Lajami, A. Al-Faraj, I. Gueye, E. Millot, Ó. Rodríguez, C. Diandy, G. Laborde, M. F. Al-Nemer

Prediction:

**Al-Nassr 2–0 Diriyah** — the hosts' quality should break through a patchy visitor's defence. 🎯

**Qingdao in total freefall, Beijing looking sharp** — one team's spiraling hard, the other keeps finding ways to avoid defeat. 🔴

Qingdao are 0-5 in their last five, leaking goals and looking lost. Beijing have 2W3D in the same stretch and boast the superior recent track record, winning 8 of their last 17 H2H meetings against Hainiu.

Key storylines:

- **Qingdao's defense is hemorrhaging** — they've conceded at least one goal in every recent outing, with heavy losses to Wuhan Three Towns (1-5) and Shanghai Port. Beijing will smell blood.

- **Beijing's draw-heavy form** — three draws in five games shows decent resilience but also a lack of clinical finishing when it matters. If they can't convert chances, Qingdao might scrape something.

- **Hainiu's attacking lifeline** — **C. Strandberg** and **S. Wenjie** are their main spears up top; they need service and clinical conversion to threaten Beijing's defense.

- **M. Ferrier and G. Fernandes under pressure**: Incheon's attacking pair need a spark, or Pohang's defense will suffocate them.
